title: Enhancing Robustness of Offline Reinforcement Learning Under Data Corruption via Sharpness-Aware Minimization (Student Abstract)
publication_status_observed: Accepted as Oral Presentation at AAAI 2026 Student Abstract and Poster Program (SAPP); arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.17568v1
main_claims: Data corruption in offline RL creates sharp minima in the loss landscape, leading to poor generalization and policy degradation.
Applying SAM as a plug-and-play optimizer for the value function network in IQL and RIQL consistently improves performance under both random and adversarial data corruption.
SAM finds smoother reward surfaces in offline RL settings, visually confirmed through reward surface visualization.
methodology: SAM is integrated as a wrapper optimizer replacing Adam for the value function (V-function) network in IQL and RIQL baselines. Experiments are conducted on three D4RL continuous control environments (halfcheetah, walker2d, hopper) under random and adversarial observation and mixture corruptions (30% corruption rate, 3 seeds). Ablation studies identify the V-function as the optimal application target.
key_results: SAM raises average normalized score from 34.47 to 44.40 for IQL under random corruption, and from 22.45 to 36.03 under adversarial corruption.
SAM raises RIQL average from 33.97 to 39.47 under random corruption.
Applying SAM to V-function only (best configuration) yields average score of 29.03 vs baseline RIQL 26.03 in ablation.
limitations: Experiments limited to D4RL continuous control; generalization to other offline RL settings unknown.
Student abstract format; limited methodological detail and theoretical justification.
ρ requires environment-specific tuning, limiting plug-and-play generalizability.
relevance_to_rq: This paper applies SAM in offline RL to improve robustness under input corruption, paralleling the RQ's interest in SAM for OOD generalization. While the domain (RL) differs from image classification, the mechanism (SAM seeking flat loss minima to improve robustness to corrupted inputs) directly relates to the flatness-vs-robustness decomposition in the RQ.
